Wooden High School]] POY (2011) }} '''Spencer Dinwiddie''' is an American [[basketball]] player who recently completed his college career for the [[Colorado Buffaloes men's basketball]] team. The California native was known to be an elite high school athlete when he attended [[William Howard Taft Charter High School (Los Angeles)|William Howard Taft High School]] in [[Woodland Hills, California]]. == High school career == Playing basketball for the [[William Howard Taft High School (Los Angeles)|William Howard Taft High School]] Toreadors, Dinwiddie was one of the most talented high school stars the school had seen since [[Jordan Farmar]] in 2003. By the end of his senior year at Taft High School, he was averaging 11.2 points, 7.7 assists, 3.1 rebounds, and 2.4 steals per game. With the help from two other college basketball hopefuls, [[DeAndre Daniels]] and [[Bryce Jones]], Dinwiddie and Taft High School found themselves winning the city championship in 2011. Following this accomplishment, many more were waiting. He was named the [[Los Angeles City Section]] Player of the Year and ultimately the John R. Wooden High School Player of the Year, making him just one of the seven players before him that won the award as a senior.[http://www.cubuffs.com/ViewArticle.dbml?ATCLID=205185490 Spencer Dinwiddie Bio] As a three-star recruit by [[Rivals.com]], Dinwiddie was ranked the 25th best point guard prospect and 146th best recruit in the nation for his class. He eventually chose to play for the [[Colorado Buffaloes men's basketball|Colorado Buffaloes]] over other possibilities such as [[Harvard Crimson men's basketball|Harvard]], [[Oregon Ducks men's basketball|Oregon]], [[UCLA Bruins men's basketball|UCLA]], and [[UNLV Rebels basketball|UNLV]]. == College career == === Freshman === After becoming a part of the Colorado Buffaloes program, Dinwiddie finished the season averaging 10.0 points, 3.6 rebounds, and 1.8 assists. Although he was the fourth-leading scorer on his new team, the Buffaloes had four players finishing the season with a scoring average in double digits. Despite his lack of scoring ability, Dinwiddie was the only [[2011–12 Pacific-12 Conference men's basketball season|Pac-12]] freshman to shoot for a field-goal percentage of over 40% that season. Leading the Buffaloes in free-throw percentage was one of the more skilled free-throw shooting freshman, ranking third among all players with his amount of college basketball experience.[http://espn.go.com/mens-college-basketball/team/stats/_/id/38/year/2012/colorado-buffaloes Colorado Buffaloes 2011-12 Statistics] He also helped a regularly ineffective Colorado team finally earned its first NCAA Tournament berth since the 2002-03. As the season came to a close, Dinwiddie was named to the Pac-12 All-Freshman Team along with several other big names such as [[Tony Wroten]] of the [[Washington Huskies men's basketball|Washington Huskies]]. === Sophomore === When [[Carlon Brown]] left the team and began playing for the [[Santa Cruz Warriors]] of the [[NBA Development League]], Spencer Dinwiddie rapidly rose to the top of the scoring list for the Buffaloes. He finished the season averaging 15.3 points, 3.2 rebounds, and 3.0 assists per game, also leading the team in assists. Again, Dinwiddie helped Colorado reach their second consecutive NCAA Tournament berth, something the program could not manage in years. As the season continued, he and teammate [[Askia Booker]] were widely known to be one of the most dangerous backcourts in all of Division I college basketball. === Junior === Spencer Dinwiddie continued to play his role as the leader of the [[Colorado Buffaloes men's basketball]] team as his junior year began. The Buffaloes made a widely publicized "[[Cinderella (sports)|Cinderella Story]]", winning 14 of their first 16 regular season games, most notable toppling a successful [[Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball|Kansas Jayhawks]] due to a game-winner from [[Askia Booker]]. Dinwiddie was considered to be the foundation of this unexpected run. On January 12, 2014, Spencer Dinwiddie suffered an [[Anterior cruciate ligament|ACL]] injury, forcing him to sit out for the remainder of the season, against [[Washington Huskies men's basketball|Washington]]. Without Dinwiddie, the program seemingly crumbled, finishing the season just 7-8.[http://espn.go.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/10288706/colorado-buffaloes-star-spencer-dinwiddie-season Colorado Buffaloes Star Spencer Dinwiddie out for season] == International career == In the [[2013 Summer Universiade]] in [[Kazan, Russia]], Dinwiddie represented the [[United States]]. Although [[Russia at the 2013 Summer Universiade|Russia]], the host nation, emerged as the gold medalists, Spencer Dinwiddie set the [[Summer Universiade]] record for the highest assists average after playing in eight games. == References == {{Reflist}} {{United States Men Basketball Squad 2013 Summer Universiade}} {{Persondata | NAME = Dinwiddie, Spencer | ALTERNATIVE NAMES = | SHORT DESCRIPTION = American basketball player | DATE OF BIRTH = 1993-04-06 | PLACE OF BIRTH = [[Woodland Hills, California]] | DATE OF DEATH = | PLACE OF DEATH = }} {{DEFAULTSORT:Dinwiddie, Spencer}} [[Category:1993 births]] [[Category:Living people]] [[Category:Basketball players from California]] [[Category:Colorado Buffaloes men's basketball players]] [[Category:People from Woodland Hills, Los Angeles]] [[Category:Point guards]] [[Category:Sportspeople from Los Angeles, California]]
